title: Prawn Stir-Fry
subtitle: Quick garlic and ginger prawn stir-fry with noodles
excerpt: Raw king prawns stir-fried at high heat with garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and vegetables, served over egg noodles. Ready in 15 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Prawn stir-fries are a staple of Chinese takeaway menus across the UK. The home version is faster than delivery and better for it: fresh prawns have a cleaner, sweeter flavour than those that have been sitting in a sauce. The high heat is essential; the sauce is added right at the end and takes only seconds to reduce and coat everything. Have everything measured and ready before the wok goes on the heat.

recipeTools.notes: Or a large frying pan over the highest heat.

content.text: Cook the noodles first and keep them warm. The stir-fry itself takes under 8 minutes. Prawns go in last and are pulled off the heat the moment they are pink all the way through.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions. Drain and set aside. Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornflour slurry in a small bowl.
Heat the wok until smoking. Add the oil. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add the pak choi and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the prawns. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, tossing, until pink all the way through.
Pour in the sauce. Toss for 30 seconds until it thickens and coats everything. Divide the noodles between bowls. Spoon the prawn stir-fry over the top. Scatter with spring onion and chilli flakes.
